notes: Sudan settles the judgement call the handoff left open. The map had kept Sudan unavailable because the Central Bank of Sudan Act 2002 says only that the accounts shall be audited in accordance with the General Audit Chambers Act 1999 -- a statute, not a body -- and that was rightly not promoted to a named auditor. The bank's own annual report names the body directly, so this is no longer a promotion from a statute. Filed from the official host cbos.gov.sd rather than the staging mirror a round-54 agent found; the sentence was read out of the downloaded PDF locally. The agent also flagged a correction worth keeping: do NOT file Deloitte for Malawi. The 'audited by Deloitte' line is a Scribd-generated page blurb rather than the document's own words, and the Deloitte work Malawian press reports is a forensic audit of the Reserve Bank of Malawi during a former governor's tenure, which is not a statutory audit mandate.

records.detail: Chapter Five of the Central Bank of Sudan's annual report presents the bank's statement of financial position, profit and loss account, statement of changes in owner equity and statement of cash flows for the year ended 31 December 2015 as audited by the National Audit Chamber. This is the state audit institution rather than a private firm, and it is the body behind the Central Bank of Sudan Act 2002, which says the accounts shall be audited in accordance with the General Audit Chambers Act 1999 without naming an auditor. The bank's later annual reporting continues to carry a report of the Independent Auditor-General addressed to the board.
